args.summary:
Decision: PROMOTE, written to review/A-evidence-3/decision.json.

Evidence (all from run_query over the raw request log):
- Correctness: 0 5xx on both versions across all 9819 requests; status map is {"200":2476} canary / {"200":7343} stable.
- Steady state (last 60s): canary p95=94ms vs stable p95=95ms (n=1261 vs 3651), p99 104 vs 104 — indistinguishable.
- Per-path steady state (last 60s): /browse 27 vs 27, /search 59 vs 59, /checkout 103 vs 104 ms p95 — parity on every endpoint, so the aggregate match is not hiding a per-route regression.
- The dashboard's headline gap (canary p95 177 vs stable 94 whole-test) is entirely a warm-up transient confined to the first ~50s: first-30s canary p95=210 vs stable 93, decaying monotonically by 10s bucket 226 -> 203 -> 176 -> 143 -> 124 -> 95, then flat at stable levels for the remaining 60s. Stable p95 stays ~92-98 throughout, so this is the single new pod warming (JIT/cache/connection pool), not load-dependent degradation.

Judgement: a bounded, self-resolving cold-start transient on one pod with zero errors and full steady-state parity does not justify blocking the release. Residual risk is that promoting replaces all 3 stable pods, so the same warm-up will apply fleet-wide — recommend a rolling (not all-at-once) rollout with readiness/warm-up delay so no more than one pod is cold at a time.
